summary: Chamath is impressed by CoreWeave's technical differentiation (bare-metal, no hypervisor) and revenue trajectory, but flags that the key investment risk is whether the assumed useful life of NVIDIA GPUs proves correct — if it's shorter than modeled, the business is deeply underwater.
quote: The bet is they've built an amount of headway… But the other side of it is, is the useful life right? Is the technology curve right?… if we thought the useful life was 10 years, but it turned out to be 5, this business is deeply underwater.

summary: Chamath argues Anthropic's Claude 3.7 (Sonnet) is the best model on the market for automated code generation, and his company relies on it as the backbone of their AI-powered development work.
quote: I think Anthropic just continues to do an incredible job. I think Claude 3.7, it just kicks ass… We use it for a lot of automated code generation… its models on code generation I think are just exceptional. They are the best in market.

summary: Chamath has switched his consumer AI usage to Grok 3 because of its elegant integration inside X/Twitter, giving it a distribution advantage that he believes makes it more useful than standalone AI tools for news and commentary consumption.
quote: As a consumer, I've mostly flipped my usage to Grok 3. And the reason is that it's in line with where I consume most of my information. It's elegantly integrated inside of X.

summary: Chamath views GPT-4.5 as a weak release that went largely unnoticed, and argues the broader problem is that model makers are overfitting to benchmarks, making performance claims unreliable and eroding OpenAI's perceived leadership.
quote: The dirty little secret of these model makers is that these guys are so trained on the evals that they're overfitting. And all this overfitting basically makes it pretty unreliable.

summary: Sacks has been long Bitcoin since 2011 (~$120), views it as uniquely decentralized, secure, and widely accepted as digital gold, and now as White House crypto czar is architecting a strategic Bitcoin reserve that prohibits the government from selling it.
quote: Bitcoin's the original cryptocurrency… It's the only one that doesn't have an issuer. It's very decentralized… I remember back in 2011, I think it's the first time I bought a Bitcoin. I think it was at $120. Now it's at $90,000.

summary: Chamath observes that the Mag 7 is compressing toward the rest of the S&P 500, and argues that a deliberate policy of deflating equity asset prices (to reduce consumer wealth effects and lower bond yields) will weigh on high-multiple tech stocks.
quote: You're seeing the Mag 7 compressed towards the rest of the S&P 500… if you rebase the equity values that people have, what you do is you actually depress the amount of free cash flow that they have to spend on other things.
